Information About Robot Access to our Pages
The Project Gutenberg website is intended for human users only.
Any perceived use of automated tools to access the Project Gutenberg website will result in a temporary or permanent block of your IP address. The only exceptions to this rule are below.
Contents
How to Get All Ebook Files

How to Get all Ebook Files
The best way to have a local up-to-date copy of all files is to setup a private mirror: See:
the Mirroring How-To
How to Get Certain Ebook files
wget
is free software and available for Linux, Windows, and Mac OS X at
www.gnu.org/software/wget/
This is an example of how to get files using wget:
wget -w 2 -m -H "https://www.gutenberg.org/robot/harvest?filetypes[]=html"
Replace html with the file type you are interested in.
html
txt
epub.images
epub.noimages
kindle.images
kindle.noimages
mp3
If you want only files in a given language say:
wget -w 2 -m -H "https://www.gutenberg.org/robot/harvest?filetypes[]=html&langs[]=de"
Replace ‘de’ with the ISO language code you are interested in. Tip: you can learn the language code of any language in the Project Gutenberg catalog by looking at the status window of your browser while moving your cursor over the language at
this page

Mirroring How-To
How to Get Catalog Data
You can extract the whole Project Gutenberg catalog data from the
Project Gutenberg catalog in machine-readable format
. The catalog data are granted to the public domain.
Files change frequently
Project Gutenberg publishes hundreds of new eBooks every month, and we also fix hundreds of books when issues like typos are reported. In addition, the ‘generated’ formats (under the ‘cache’ top-level directory) are re-built monthly and sometimes have changes due to improvements in the software that builds them.
When you save a copy of a Project Gutenberg eBook, consider periodically checking for any changes.

OAPEN Library metadata
OAPEN Library metadata
OAPEN enables libraries and aggregators to use the metadata of all available titles in the OAPEN Library for free.
The metadata is available in the following formats:
MARCXML – based on the MARC 21 XML Schema, can be converted easily using MARCEdit
OAPENLibrary_MARCXML.xml
: The contents of the OAPEN Library in MARCXML format
OAPENLibrary_MARCXML_books.xml
: All records describing books of the OAPEN Library that contain a download link, in MARCXML format
OAPENLibrary_MARCXML_chapters.xml
: All records describing chapters of the OAPEN Library that contain a download link, in MARCXML format
OAPENLibrary_MARCXML_no_links.xml
: All records of the OAPEN Library that do not contain a download link, in MARCXML format
Penn State University Libraries provides MARC21 records created from MARCXML metadata supplied by OAPEN. Download the data here:
https://dx.doi.org/10.26207/9w9c-jc15
.
KBART – tab delimited text file
OAPENLibrary_KBART.tsv
: Metadata of the OAPEN Library in KBART format - separated with TAB characters
OAPENLibrary_KBART_books.tsv
: Metadata of the books in the OAPEN Library in KBART format - separated with TAB characters
ONIX (3.0) – XML
OAPENLibrary_ONIX.xml
: OAPEN Library export in ONIX file format
JSON – JavaScript Object Notation
OAPENLibrary.json
: All full text titles of the OAPEN Library as a JSON file
CSV – comma delimited text file
OAPENLibrary.csv
: OAPEN metadata in CSV format
RIS – Research Information Systems
RIS metadata download
OAI PMH harvesting
The base URL for OAI-PMH harvesting is https://library.oapen.org/oai/
(Example:
https://library.oapen.org/oai/request?verb=ListMetadataFormats
)
There are several metadata formats available. The xoai format lists all metadata fields, see
https://library.oapen.org/oai/request?verb=ListRecords&metadataPrefix=xoai
.
(Example:
https://library.oapen.org/oai/request?verb=GetRecord&identifier=oai:library.oapen.org:20.500.12657/25287&metadataPrefix=xoai
)
RSS and Atom feeds
RSS 1.0
RSS 2.0
Atom
All metadata feeds are available under a
CC0 1.0 license
.
Selective Export
It is also possible to make use of our ‘Selective Export’ functionality. This enables you to export metadata in a flexible way: first by selecting the relevant titles and secondly by choosing the export format. The selective export functionality makes it easier for specialist libraries, subject repositories and frequent users to only retrieve specified subsets of open access books according to their preferences - for instance by publisher or subject field. Please be aware that this export function is optimised for sets up to 500 titles. More information can be found
here

Ebook Feeds
We offer several ebook feeds that you can use in your ereading app to browse, search, and download from our catalog. You can also add our feeds to your RSS client to get notified of new ebooks as they’re released, or to browse our catalog from your feed reader.
How to access the feeds
Our
New Releases RSS/Atom ebook feeds
are open to everyone.
Access to our other feeds is a benefit of
membership in our Patrons Circle
. You can also get access in one of the following ways:
Join the Patrons Circle
by making a small donation in support of our mission. Patrons have full access to our ebook feeds for the duration of their gift.
Produce an ebook
for Standard Ebooks to get lifetime access to our ebook feeds. (If you’ve already done that,
contact us
to enable your access.)
Corporate sponsors
get access to all of our ebook feeds for the duration of their sponsorship.
Contact us
to chat about having your organization sponsor our mission.
If you’re a Patrons Circle member, when prompted enter your email address and leave the password field blank to access an ebook feed.
OPDS feeds
OPDS feeds
can be added to ereading apps on phones and tablets to search, browse, and download from our ebook catalog, directly in your ereader. Many ereading apps support OPDS feeds.
See our article on
how to add an OPDS feed to your ereader
.
The Standard Ebooks OPDS feed
https://standardebooks.org/feeds/opds
To get an OPDS 2.0 feed, set the
Accept
HTTP header to
application/opds+json
.
RSS/Atom feeds
These feeds can be read by any modern
RSS reader
.
Note that some RSS readers may show ebooks ordered by when they were last updated, even though the feeds are ordered by ebooks were first released. You should be able to change this sort order in your RSS reader.
